name: Benefits Enrollment Agent
headline: Guide every employee through enrollment without making their benefits decisions for them
pitch: Give employees a conversational guide to the enrollment window, life-event rules, plan costs for their tier, provider networks, missing documents, and a draft election, while eligibility, plan choice, and submission stay with the employee and benefits staff.
why_try: The demo lets a employee ask a natural question and receive a source-backed, reviewable answer with the approval boundary visible in the response.
customer_challenge: Employees miss life-event windows, compare plans by hand, and discover network gaps too late, while benefits staff answer the same questions all season.
microsoft_ai_story: Copilot Studio and Microsoft Teams give employees a conversational front door; approved benefits administration and carrier directory sources can be bound with identity, row-level access, data minimization, and audit controls.
business_value: Helps employees act within open enrollment and life-event windows.
Makes plan costs and provider networks easy to compare for each employee.
Reduces routine enrollment questions for benefits staff.
business_flow: Employee submission and benefits staff review

capabilities.name: Enrollment window explanation
capabilities.purpose: Use when an employee asks when open enrollment opens or closes, how many days are left, or what can change.

capabilities.name: Life-event change rules
capabilities.purpose: Use when an employee states a life event such as a new child, marriage, loss of other coverage, or divorce and asks what can change and by when.

capabilities.name: Plan cost comparison
capabilities.purpose: Use when an employee asks to compare medical plan costs, deductibles, out-of-pocket maximums, and networks for their coverage tier.

capabilities.name: Provider network check
capabilities.purpose: Use when an employee asks whether their doctors or clinics are in network on each plan.

capabilities.name: Document checklist
capabilities.purpose: Use when an employee or benefits specialist asks which supporting documents are received, missing, and when they are due.

capabilities.name: Election draft preview
capabilities.purpose: Use when an employee asks to draft or preview election changes; the draft stays Not Submitted and shows the per-paycheck cost change.

capabilities.name: Personal deadline list
capabilities.purpose: Use when an employee asks which benefits deadlines are coming up and in what order.

prompts.label: Employee: Enrollment window explanation
prompts.prompt: When does open enrollment close, and what can I change?

recorded_answer.prompt: When does open enrollment close, and what can I change?
recorded_answer.answer:
Open enrollment closes **Nov 20, 2026** (10 days left), with elections effective Jan 1, 2027.

During this window you can:
- Switch medical plans (Core HMO, Choice PPO, Saver HDHP)
- Add/remove dependents or change coverage tier
- Elect health/dependent care spending accounts for 2027
- Update life insurance beneficiaries

Heads up: if you do nothing, your current medical/dental/vision carry over automatically — but spending account elections do **not** roll over, so you'd need to re-elect those if you want them in 2027.

Want me to compare the three medical plans or check if any documents are missing?

prompts.label: Employee: Life-event change rules
prompts.prompt: We just had a baby. What benefit changes can I make, and by when?

recorded_answer.prompt: We just had a baby. What benefit changes can I make, and by when?
recorded_answer.answer:
Congrats! 🎉 Here's what you can do:

**Window:** You have until **Nov 27, 2026** (30 days from the birth date) to submit changes.

**What you can change:**
- Add your child to medical, dental, and vision
- Move to a higher coverage tier
- Start or adjust a dependent care spending account
- Update life insurance beneficiaries

**Documents needed:**
- Birth certificate (or adoption decree)
- Child's name and date of birth

**Form:** Life Event Change Request (LE-1)

Coverage would start retroactive to the birth date (Oct 28, 2026) once processed.

One more thing: open enrollment for the general 2027 plan choice closes **Nov 20, 2026** — separate from this, but worth handling together if you're already reviewing plans. Want me to pull up a plan cost comparison or check if your pediatrician is in-network?

prompts.label: Employee: Plan cost comparison
prompts.prompt: Compare the three medical plans for family coverage.

recorded_answer.prompt: Compare the three medical plans for family coverage.
recorded_answer.answer:
Here's the family coverage comparison for 2027:

| Plan | Per Paycheck | Annual Premium | Deductible | OOP Max | Network |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Core HMO** | $142 | $3,692 | $1,000 | $7,000 | Core network |
| **Choice PPO** | $218 | $5,668 | $1,500 | $8,000 | Broad network |
| **Saver HDHP** | $89 | $2,314 | $3,400 | $10,000 | Broad network (+$1,500 employer HSA seed) |

**Quick take:**
- **Cheapest premium:** Saver HDHP, but highest deductible/OOP max before the HSA seed offsets it
- **Broadest network with lowest deductible:** Choice PPO, but costs the most per paycheck
- **Middle ground:** Core HMO — lower premium than PPO, smaller network than PPO/HDHP

This is cost info only — I'm not recommending which one fits your situation. Want me to check if your doctors are in-network for any of these?

prompts.label: Employee: Provider network check
prompts.prompt: Are Lakeside Family Clinic and Riverbend Pediatrics in network on each plan?

recorded_answer.prompt: Are Lakeside Family Clinic and Riverbend Pediatrics in network on each plan?
recorded_answer.answer:
Here's the network status for both:

| Provider | Core HMO | Choice PPO | Saver HDHP |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Lakeside Family Clinic** | ✅ In network | ✅ In network | ✅ In network |
| **Riverbend Pediatrics** | ❌ Out of network | ✅ In network | ✅ In network |

**Key takeaway:** If you need Riverbend Pediatrics, the Core HMO won't cover it in-network — Choice PPO or Saver HDHP would. Worth double-checking with the carrier directly since networks can shift for the 2027 plan year.

prompts.label: Employee: Document checklist
prompts.prompt: What documents do I still need to send?

recorded_answer.prompt: What documents do I still need to send?
recorded_answer.answer:
You still need to submit one document:

- **Birth certificate or adoption decree** — not yet received

Due by **Nov 27, 2026**, along with your Life Event Change Request (form LE-1, already drafted and ready for your review). Upload it through the official benefits portal — not here.

recorded_answer.prompt: Draft my election changes, but don't submit anything.
recorded_answer.answer:

- **Request deadline**: Nov 27, 2026

prompts.label: Employee: Personal deadline list
prompts.prompt: What benefits deadlines should I put on my calendar?

recorded_answer.prompt: What benefits deadlines should I put on my calendar?
recorded_answer.answer:
Here's what to mark on your calendar:

- **Nov 20, 2026** — Open enrollment closes (2027 medical plan choice + spending account elections)
- **Nov 27, 2026** — Deadline for life event change requests/documents (e.g., birth/adoption)
- **Jan 1, 2027** — New elections take effect

The big one is **Nov 20** — only 10 days out. If you've got a life event (new baby, marriage, etc.) in play, let me know and I can walk you through what's needed.
